name: Jiji Sugi and Baba Sugi of Suwa Shrine (Grandpa Cedar and Grandma Cedar)

location.address: 137 Machiya, Natsui, Ono Town, Tamura District, Fukushima Prefecture, within the grounds of Suwa Shrine

access: Free, shrine grounds, flanking the approach path (Jiji-sugi on the right/east facing the main hall, Baba-sugi on the left/west). 5-minute walk from Natsui Station (JR Ban'etsu East Line); about 15 min by car from Ono IC (Ban'etsu Expressway), or a 10-minute taxi from Ono-Shinmachi Station.
transport: Natsui Station (JR Ban'etsu East Line), 5-minute walk.
verify_notes: REAL PLACE: Ono Town, Tamura District, not Miharu; a third distinct municipality among these four leads. TWO separately named, physically adjacent trees, not one: 翁スギ (Okina-sugi/Jiji-sugi, 'Grandpa Cedar', the taller/thicker of the two, standing right/east of the shrine approach) and 媼スギ (Omina-sugi/Baba-sugi, 'Grandma Cedar', left/west), their trunks only about 1.37m apart at the base with a small ground-level difference of about 1.1m between them. Locally called a 'married couple' pair (meoto-sugi). This is a genuine compact famous ensemble with one obvious place to stand between them, not a scattered avenue, so it should ship as ONE collectible entry describing both trees rather than two separate pages. National Natural Monument since 21 December 1937, following a field survey by the botanist Manabu Miyoshi on 10 October 1936. Legend (shrine tradition, not independently dated) says they were hand-planted as saplings in 780 CE by Fujiwara no Tsuguna, who built the shrine to pray for victory in a military campaign; treat this as legend/tradition in the story, not as a documented planting date (per the bridge-claim trap, do not present 780 CE as a proven age). Dimensions: Jiji-sugi height 48.5m, girth 9.2m at breast height (1.5m), root girth ~10.6m; Baba-sugi height 47.8m, girth 9.5m, root girth ~10.85m. Recorded girth_cm as 920 (Jiji-sugi's figure, the slightly smaller of the two, as a conservative single number); the writer should ideally give both trees' figures rather than collapsing to one. Age sources disagree mildly: town page and most sources say 1,200 years, one source frames it as 1,100-1,200; used that range. Vitality: ja.Wikipedia explicitly describes 'vigorous vitality' with no visible major damage or decline on either tree, the healthiest-looking candidate of the four alongside Sugisawa. A 2008 public-domain photo (uploader Yauchi) and a 25 Oct 2023 CC BY photo of the site signboard (same photographer, Sakaori, as the other three leads) both confirm the site; the signboard photo is geotagged to 37°15'18.1"N 140°39'36.58"E, converting to the exact lead coordinates, so tree-level precision is solid even though the coordinate is technically of the signboard rather than of a single trunk (there are two trunks here regardless).
